entities.summary:
August Ludwig Ferdinand Count von Nostitz-Ransen was a Prussian general who served as adjutant general to Frederick William III of Prussia from 1790 to 1800. He played a crucial role in the Prussian army's modernization efforts, implementing reforms that improved the discipline and training of the military. Von Nostitz-Ransen's efforts contributed to Prussia's emergence as a major military power in Europe during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

Born in 1768, von Nostitz-Ransen graduated from the Prussian War Academy in Berlin and quickly rose through the ranks of the Prussian army. His military career was marked by several key victories, including the Battle of Jena in 1806, where he led the Prussian forces to a decisive victory over Napoleon's army.

Von Nostitz-Ransen died on May 28, 1866, at the age of 98, leaving behind a legacy as one of Prussia's most prominent military leaders.

The von Nostitz-Ransen Museum in Berlin commemorates his life and achievements, featuring exhibits on his military campaigns and the modernization of the Prussian army.
